transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-11 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Markus Leung (WillowCreek CTO), Aisha Romero (ML Eng), Sanjay Patel (Head of Security), Li Yan (Infra)

Summary: quick intro, high level goals, deep dive into their current stack (OpenAI API + in-house vLLM/TGI for on-prem), discussion of eval parity approach and a pilot plan; closed with agreed next steps and owners.

[00:00] Jordan Miles: Hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Jordan, i'm the AE on this account, with me is Priya our SE. how's everyone doing?
[00:09] Markus Leung: hey hey doing well thanks. we got a tight agenda, want to make sure we cover compliance and the parity tests.
[00:15] Priya Desai: great, we'll run through high level, then dig into the vllm/tgi side and what parity looks like.
[00:22] Aisha Romero: quick note, we currently run OpenAI for prod in most user flows but we host some heavy batch scoring on our infra using vLLM + TGI for cost reasons.
[00:34] Sanjay Patel: and from security side, we need SOC2 + key rotation, KMS integration, and audit logs — also data residency for EU customers.
[00:45] Jordan Miles: understood — thanks. so rough first question, what are your success criteria for a migration or pilot?
[00:51] Markus Leung: parity on responses for our golden prompts, under 120ms median latency for our single-turn support flows, and predictable unit cost - preferably less than current TCO by 20% in batch jobs.
[01:10] Priya Desai: parity is doable but we have to define metrics: exact-match, semantic similarity, and business-logic correctness. we'll propose an eval harness.
[01:22] Aisha Romero: we've got about 5k golden prompts, mixture of few-shot and system messages. they need to be preserved exactly.
[01:30] [01:30] Speaker 2: yeah so for the vllm steps, is Redwood able to run the same kernels/quant configs — we did a lot of int8 quantization in-house.
[01:42] Priya Desai: short answer: yes, we support multiple quant profiles and can run int8 or mixed precision variants. we do automatic kernel selection in the runtime but we'll replicate your config in a pilot. there may be small tokenization differences depending on model variant.
[01:58] Markus Leung: tokenization differences are a big concern — last time we ported a model we saw slight reply drift because of token boundary changes.
[02:06] Jordan Miles: good flag. part of the parity run will include token-level diffs, and we can run the exact same model weights if you'd like us to ingest them into a private tenant. for hosted we typically use our verified model catalog but for private we can do exact weight hosting.
[02:24] Li Yan: how about vLLM compatibility — can you spin up TGI endpoints or does Redwood require model conversion?
[02:31] Priya Desai: we can accept TGI/vLLM checkpoints; sometimes a light conversion is needed (dtype/kv cache layout), but we handle that. for dedicated hosts we keep the same runtime semantics; for private on-prem we can bundle vLLM compatible runtime.
[02:51] Aisha Romero: cool. and latency — hosted vs dedicated vs private, what differences should we expect?
[02:58] Priya Desai: hosted gives fastest onboarding and predictable bursts, dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower median latency because you control capacity, private depends on your infra - with good GPUs you can get parity with dedicated but you lose our autoscaling benefits.
[03:16] Sanjay Patel: on compliance, we need SSO (SAML/Okta), KMS/HSM integration, and per-request audit logs retained for 1 year. do you support per-tenant log export?
[03:29] Jordan Miles: yes - we support SAML SSO, KMS integrations (AWS/GCP/Azure) and can stream audit logs to customer SIEMs; retention is configurable and exportable.
[03:38] Markus Leung: Any gotchas on data residency? some traffic must stay in eu-west-1.
[03:43] Priya Desai: we'll route requests to region-specific endpoints or run private deployment in that region. for hosted we have EU regions, dedicated can be pinned, and private obviously you control physical location.
[03:56] [03:56] Speaker 1: what about costs for batch scoring - we currently do 100M tokens/mo in batch, most of it offline on vLLM.
[04:06] Jordan Miles: for large batch, dedicated or private is usually the most economic; Redwood Optimize can recommend batching/kv cache configs to lower token costs. we'll run cost modeling as part of the pilot.
[04:21] Aisha Romero: our infra team also cares about GPU types; we're mostly on A100s and a few H100 dev boxes. can Redwood take H100s for lower latency on long sequences?
[04:33] Priya Desai: yes we support both, and we choose kernels based on hardware and sequence length distribution. for long context we often prefer tensor core optimized kernels available on H100.
[04:47] Markus Leung: bench strategy: we'd like to reproduce our current p95 and median latencies and LL eval score. how long does the bench take?
[04:56] Priya Desai: depends on size - for a 5k prompt golden set with a few-shot context, plan 24–48 hours to gather stable stats across variants. we'll run hosted and dedicated parity runs and provide a spreadsheet with token-level breakdown.
[05:12] Li Yan: any friction importing our model weights? we have internal licensing for a tuned LLaMA derivative.
[05:20] Jordan Miles: we'll need license confirmation but we can host the weights in a private tenant or on private deployment; legal can attach an NDA if necessary.
[05:30] Aisha Romero: what about the eval harness - do you have a standard?
[05:34] Priya Desai: yes we use a harness that computes exact match, bertscore, and a customized business-rule check. we can run your golden prompts and return per-prompt diffs plus aggregated metrics.
[05:46] Sanjay Patel: i want to flag data lifecycle: how long do you keep cached KV states, are there purge controls?
[05:54] Priya Desai: KV cache is ephemeral per-request unless you enable prefix caching for speedups; we have purge and retention settings and can disable caching for regulated flows.
[06:06] Markus Leung: okay sensible. can we talk about pilot length and success gates?
[06:11] Jordan Miles: typical pilot is 3–4 weeks: week 1 ingest + config, week 2 parity runs, week 3 integration and SLA tuning. success gates: parity within agreed thresholds and cost model acceptance.
[06:24] Aisha Romero: do you support == function / tool calling? we rely on structured outputs.
[06:29] Priya Desai: yes we support function calling, streaming and structured output; will validate against your schema.
[06:36] [06:36] Speaker 2: small Q, is there any lag in function call fidelity compared to OpenAI? we've noticed subtle JSON formatting changes with other runtimes.
[06:47] Priya Desai: we test structured output and can include schema conformance checks in the harness. usually it's more about prompt phrasing than runtime but we'll validate.
[06:57] Jordan Miles: ok let's cover deliverables. we'll share security docs, pilot proposal and a pricing sheet. Priya will own the benchmark plan. Markus will surface the golden prompts and confirm POC stakeholders.
[07:09] Markus Leung: sounds good. timeline wise, we'd like to start next week if we can.
[07:14] Jordan Miles: we can start ingestion next Tue - I'll follow up with proposed slots for the 48 hour bench.
[07:20] Aisha Romero: one more thing - do you have a recommended quantization profile for batch scoring? our current int8 gave a ~1.8x speedup.
[07:30] Priya Desai: we'll propose a mixed-int8 profile for batch and a higher precision for low-latency paths; the benchmark will test both and report quality tradeoffs.
[07:42] Sanjay Patel: also we need contract-level SLAs for dedicated deployments - 99.9% uptime and defined latency SLOs.
[07:51] Jordan Miles: we offer SLA-backed dedicated plans; legal will include SLO terms in the pilot contract.
[07:58] Li Yan: final question - monitoring hooks and traces?
[08:02] Priya Desai: we provide per-route dashboards, traces, and token-level cost breakdowns; you can ingest traces via our tracing hooks.
[08:14] [08:14] Speaker 1: that all sounds good, thank you.
[08:17] Jordan Miles: thanks everyone - quick recap of next steps now.
